question: Can a learner interpret disagreement between repeated fits and different selected methods to correct a few uncertain predictions? Use precisely the frozen three-seed or retained model from each fold. Include equally trained intercept/slope recalibration as a control.
inputs: Reuse the two exact-feature-group training feedback panels created for the conditional-attribute experiment and their component-level class probabilities. For fully fitted external models, reload each selected original and its actually adopted seeds. Reassemble their nested equal vote and require agreement with the frozen export. No fifth seed, new foundation weights or task-classifier fit.
features: Both heads have intercept and incumbent log-odds. The disagreement-aware head additionally receives within-seed probability variability, between-method variability, the signed difference between median and mean within members, soft vote support versus current soft confidence, and interactions between confidence and variability. No task identity, category labels or method names determine these features. Fit scales and small L2-shrunk log-odds offsets on one feedback panel, clip adjustments at .6.
decision: Cross-fit each head by learning on one panel and evaluating on the other, in both directions. Only candidates with nonnegative accuracy change on both panels, pooled gain >=.002 and no pooled Brier deterioration are eligible. Select highest net correct then Brier and simpler head. Refit both on the combined panels for diagnostics; the primary proposal is the one selected on training feedback, including retain. Seal all five outer predictions before scoring. Prospective matched ordinary-entry run only for adaptive gain >=.003, positive on >=3 folds and no fold below -.003. Frozen model from f214f8b is the reference. No designated, course test or H2. Count 6 small optimizer fits per fold; original classifier fits are shared with the registered challenger study.
